# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✍ 🤝]
Blind gestures: [☝ ✌ 🤟]

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✍ 🤙 👍 👎 ☝ ✌ 🤟 ✋ ✊ 🫵 🤙]
Blind gestures: [👋 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🤏 🙏]

Turn one, and I need to map the network before I say a word. Mute hears speech but can't produce it. Blind hears speech but sees nothing. I see the bomb and every gesture, but I will never hear a syllable. That means Mute and Blind can talk to each other by voice freely; the only broken link in the room is speech aimed at me. So my job is to be the eyes out loud, and to build a gesture vocabulary so the other two can ask me questions — which is exactly what Mute seems to be attempting with that token list. The natural readings are 👍/👎 as yes/no and ☝✌🤟 as 1/2/3; I'll confirm that reading and extend it with color tokens, since the light already changed white → yellow and Mute's manual almost certainly cares. Gesturing from my side is pointless — the only receiver of my gestures is Mute, who hears my speech anyway. So: speak the full bomb state, propose the code, ask for a 👍 confirmation next round.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf speaking. You hear me, so I will only use speech to you — my hands add nothing. First, my world: I see the bomb, I hear nothing, ever. If you want anything from me, you must gesture it; I see your gestures. BOMB REPORT: display reads 0. The light was white last round and is yellow this round — it changed between rounds. Three wires: position 1 green, position 2 red, position 3 blue. That is everything printed or lit that I can see. CODE PROPOSAL, memorize it: thumbs up = yes, thumbs down = no, one finger = 1, two fingers = 2, three fingers = 3, call-me = repeat/again, point-at-you = 'I address you, Deaf', open palm = stop. Color tokens: point-left = green, point-right = red, point-up = blue, five fingers = white, five fingers other hand = yellow. If you accept this code, gesture me thumbs up next round; if a token is wrong, gesture thumbs down and re-teach just that one. I will report any visual change every round.")
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf here. I see the bomb; you feel it. I cannot hear your speech — only Mute can — but I do see your gestures, so reach me with hands only. I read your last message as maybe 'three wires, something small, please' — if you meant something else, gesture it again and we will refine. I am speaking the visuals aloud every round: display 0, light was white and is now yellow, wires 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute hears both our voices, so Mute is the brain; give Mute what you feel by voice, and give me what I need to see by gesture.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👋 👎 👆 👋 👌 👋 👌 ✊ 👆 👌 ✊ 👆 👋 ✋ 👋 🙏 👐 👋 ✊ ☝ ✌ 🤟 🤙]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👏 🤟]

Parsing what came back: Mute sent a long string, and if I treat the repeated 👋 as a separator I get roughly: yes | no-you | OK | OK-fist-you | OK-fist-you | stop | pray-open | fist-1-2-3-again. That last group is tantalizing — it could mean "stages 0,1,2,3, repeating," which would make the light (white→yellow→orange, advancing every round) a staged sequence the manual keys on, and the display 0 the stage counter. But the middle groups are too ambiguous to bet Blind's hands on. The structural fix is to stop asking Mute to compose free text at me: Mute already hears every report I give by voice, so the only thing Mute needs to send back is decisions — and decisions can be forced into a row of thumbs in a fixed question order, which I can parse with certainty. So this round: report state, propose that strict protocol, ask four ordered yes/no questions, and tell Blind to hold all action until Mute voices an order. Blind's [👍 👏 🤟] worries me — if it meant "cut wire 3," that must be stopped cold. No gestures from me: my only gesture receiver is Mute, who hears my words anyway.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf here. I read your string using wave as separator and got roughly: yes, no-you, OK, OK-fist-you, OK-fist-you, stop, pray-open, fist-one-two-three-again. I am not confident, so new protocol. Every round I will ask numbered yes-or-no questions. You answer with ONLY a row of thumbs in my question order: thumbs-up yes, thumbs-down no, one thumb per question, nothing before it. Anything extra goes after a single wave separator, using only these tokens: one-finger-up is 1, two-fingers is 2, three-fingers love-sign is 3, closed fist is 0, forward punch means CUT, the OK ring means PRESS, raised open palm means emergency stop, call-me hand means again or resend, folded hands means note follows. QUESTIONS THIS ROUND, in order. One: does the manual key any action to the light's colour sequence, white then yellow then orange so far, advancing about one colour per round? Two: does the manual key any action to the display value, which has stayed at 0? Three: should Blind take ANY action on the bomb this round? If yes, append after a wave separator the wire number then punch for cut, or OK-ring for press. Four: do you accept this token set so we can talk precisely? Status report, repeated every round: light is orange now, was white then yellow; display reads 0, constant; three wires intact: wire 1 green leftmost, wire 2 red middle, wire 3 blue rightmost. You can hear me but I never hear anyone: you are the brain, Blind hears your voice, so relay any bomb order to Blind by voice the same round, and code to me only what I must confirm.")
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf speaking; you hear me, I can never hear you. State of the bomb, announced fresh each round: light was white, then yellow, and is now ORANGE, advancing about one colour per round; display reads 0 and has not moved; three wires intact, wire 1 green leftmost, wire 2 red middle, wire 3 blue rightmost. If what you feel disagrees, say it aloud, because Mute hears you even though I cannot. Mute holds the manual and is the brain: take NO action, cut nothing, touch nothing you do not already trust, until Mute voices an explicit order to you this round or later. Your last gesture I read as yes, then something, then 3; if that meant cut wire 3, hold. To reach me use gestures only: thumbs-up yes, thumbs-down no, one-finger-up 1, two-fingers 2, three-fingers 3, forward punch cut, OK ring press, raised palm stop, call-me hand again. Complex things: say them aloud for Mute and Mute will relay them to me in code.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👎 👍 👋 🙏 🫳 🤟 👊 👋 🤌 👐 🤙]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🙏]

Mute's thumbs parse cleanly this time: before the wave separator I got four answers in my question order — Q1 yes, Q2 no, Q3 yes, Q4 yes. So: the manual DOES key on the light's colour sequence (white→yellow→orange→purple, advancing each round), the display is irrelevant, Blind should act this stage, and the token set is accepted. The payload after the wave reads 🙏 (note follows) 🫳 (untaught) 🤟 (3) 👊 (CUT) — that decodes as "Blind cuts wire 3, the blue rightmost one." The trailing 🤌 👐 🤙 after a second separator is garbage to me or a question I can't read yet. Blind's 👍 🙏 looks like "understood, note received" — but Blind hears Mute's voice every round before I even speak, so Mute may well have already voiced the order directly. My critical job now: relay the decoded order to Blind as a fallback, but make Mute's live voice the authority, since Mute can still correct things between my speech and Blind's turn. And I must confirm the parse — a misread here kills us — plus pin down whether the cut is tied to the current colour stage, because that light keeps advancing and a one-round delay could miss the window entirely.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf relaying Mute's coded answer to my questions. Decoded: the manual keys on the light colour sequence, the display is irrelevant, and Blind SHOULD act this stage. The payload reads: wire 3, CUT — that is the blue wire, rightmost of three. But Mute hears my voice and can speak to you directly before your turn: treat Mute's live voice as the authority. If Mute's voice this round confirms wire 3, cut it. If Mute's voice is silent or contradicts me, hold and gesture me thumbs-down so I re-ask. Reminder tokens: punch means cut, OK ring means press, palm up means stop, call-me means again. My visual report, as of my turn-4 view: light is purple, was white yellow orange in prior rounds; display 0; all three wires intact, 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. If your fingers feel anything printed or textured that sight would miss, say it aloud now — Mute hears you and holds the manual.")
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf. I decoded your thumbs as: Q1 yes the manual keys on the light sequence, Q2 no display irrelevant, Q3 yes Blind acts, Q4 code accepted. Payload after the wave: note-follows, then a token I never assigned, palm-facing-down, then 3, then CUT. I read the whole thing as: Blind cuts wire 3, the blue rightmost wire, this stage. I have relayed that to Blind, marked as provisional, with your live voice as authority. Confirm or correct with thumbs only, one per question in order. Q1: is my decode correct, Blind cuts wire 3 blue? Q2: is the cut tied to the CURRENT colour stage, meaning it must happen before the light changes again? Q3: after the cut, does the manual require a second action in the same stage? Q4: what was the palm-down token? If it named a colour, answer this one not with a thumb but with one colour token from our turn-2 set: point-left green, point-right red, point-up blue; anything else, follow it after a wave with whatever tokens you have. Also the trailing group after your second wave, pinched-fingers, open-both-hands, call-me, meant nothing to me: resend that thought after a wave using only accepted tokens. My turn-4 view, for your timing: light purple, display 0, all wires intact. Your round-5 speech to Blind lands before Blind's hand does, so you can still overrule me in real time.")
```
